articles.headline: Heat predicted to trade Bam Adebayo for $220M veteran NBA champion, six-time All-Star
keyFacts: The Miami Heat acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis in a blockbuster offseason trade.
The Heat started the season 0-4 as Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo struggled to play effectively together.
Analyst Eric Pincus proposed that Miami trade Adebayo and Tim Hardaway Jr. to the New York Knicks for Karl-Anthony Towns.
body: Coming into the season, things were looking exciting for the Miami Heat after the team made several major moves during the offseason. Following a disappointing campaign that ended without a playoff appearance, Miami entered the season with a clear goal: win a championship or consider the season a failure.
The Heat pulled off a blockbuster trade over the summer, acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis from the Milwaukee Bucks.

“The Milwaukee Bucks are trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks (including No. 13 in Tuesday's NBA draft), one pick swap and one second-round pick, sources told ESPN. The Heat are sending to Milwaukee unprotected first-rounders in 2031 and 2033 along with No. 13, a pick swap in 2030 and a 2033 second-rounder, according to sources," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.
However, the early results have been far from ideal. The Heat sit at 0-4, and Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have yet to find their rhythm as a duo.

“The Giannis and Bam fit has looked horrible — Bam looks like he has no idea what to do on offense, they’re playing too fast for what they’re talent is, they bet on Klay who looks washed…Giannis isn’t the easiest guy to play with…the Jovic extension from last year is one of the dumbest extensions given out in the last 5 years — it’s been a disaster, he’s been unplayable…10 years ago you could’ve gotten away with Giannis and Bam as your two guys…I wouldn’t bet against them figuring this out, this bad as it can get,” Bill Simmons said.

With the pairing struggling, Bleacher Report's Eric Pincus believes Miami should consider another blockbuster trade, sending Adebayo and Tim Hardaway Jr. to the New York Knicks in exchange for Karl-Anthony Towns.
“The Miami Heat receive: Karl-Anthony Towns, $6.1 million trade exception (Tim Hardaway Jr.) The New York Knicks receive: Bam Adebayo, Tim Hardaway Jr,” Pincus wrote.

Such a deal would shake up the NBA, but it seems unlikely that Miami would give up on its new duo this early in the season. Sometimes, it takes time for star players to develop chemistry, and the Heat may need to give Antetokounmpo and Adebayo more time to figure things out.

Towns is currently playing under a $220 million contract with the Knicks. If the proposed trade were to happen, his offensive skill set could make him a more natural fit alongside Antetokounmpo. Unlike a traditional big man, Towns is a threat from beyond the three-point line, which could create more spacing for Antetokounmpo to attack the basket.

articles.headline: Celtics Analyst Brian Scalabrine Just Keeps Taking Shots at 76ers Star Jaylen Brown
keyFacts: NBC Sports Boston analyst Brian Scalabrine claimed that 76ers star Jaylen Brown demanded a trade before going to Philadelphia.
A representative from Brown's team denied the trade demand report, calling it completely false.
Scalabrine later criticized Brown on multiple shows, claiming Brown wants to be the victim.
body: Celtics Analyst Brian Scalabrine Just Keeps Taking Shots at 76ers Star Jaylen Brown originally appeared on NESN .

NBC Sports Boston analyst Brian Scalabrine caused a stir on Monday when he claimed that 76ers star Jaylen Brown approached the Celtics with a trade demand before being sent to Philadelphia. A representative from Brown's team denied that the 2024 NBA Finals MVP demanded a trade, telling ESPN's Kris Rhim that the report was "10,000 percent a lie."

During Monday's pregame show, Scalabrine clarified that Brown "technically" never directly pushed for a trade. Scalabrine believed that Brown did have a list of demands, but he walked back his most shocking assertion.
Brown's denial and Scalabrine's follow-up report seemed to bring an end to the conversation around a potential trade demand. Then, Scalabrine kept talking.

On Tuesday's episode of "The Starting Lineup," Scalabrine declared that Brown "wants to be the victim in all of this." He pointed to Brown's comments about Jayson Tatum , saying that Brown is just hurting his own legacy.

When asked about his relationship with Tatum, Brown recently told reporters that Tatum has a "great PR team," adding that there is "no beef" between the former teammates but possibly "a little lamb chops and some gravy."

"He's using me, or his PR team, or whatever it is, to be the victim, and he's not gonna take responsibility for it," Scalabrine said. "That's fine. ... I just feel like he wants to say whatever he wants, and he doesn't want to be held accountable, just like on his Twitch. He wants his legacy to remain intact, and he's not gonna be responsible for the other stuff that he brings up."

articles.headline: The MultiPot XL is cleverly designed to maximize flexibility without taking up too much cupboard or counter space
keyFacts: Ninja launched the MultiPot XL multicooker, featuring a seven-liter MegaZone pot and two smaller 3.1-liter pots for cooking two different dishes simultaneously.
The appliance offers 11 cooking functions including slow cooking, searing, steaming, and sous vide, but lacks air frying and pressure cooking capabilities.
The MultiPot XL is available now from SharkNinja and major retailers with a list price of £259.99.
body: - The Ninja MultiPo XL can prepare two different dishes with different settings at the same time
- It comes with a seven-liter 'MegaZone' pot, plus two 3.1-liter pots
- It's available now for £259.99 (about $350 / AU$490)

My kitchen already contains more Ninjas than a bad kung-fu movie, all of which I've bought with my own money: Ninja has become my go-to brand thanks to clever design and decent pricing. So I'm intrigued by the launch of yet another multi-cooker, because it combines ideas from two of my favourite kitchen helpers: my multicooker and my dual-drawer air fryer.

The new multicooker is called the Ninja MultiPot XL and it comes with three pots: a seven-liter one for making big meals, and a pair of 3.1-liter ones so you can make two different things at two different settings. I thought dual-pot designs were a gimmick until I bought my air fryer, and now I'm like what's inside it: a big fan.
I've been buying multicookers since the early days of the Instant Pot, and my current multicooker model is the Ninja Foodi Max 15-in-1. It's on as I write this, making soup for the family dinner.

I love the convenience of the Max, but it's awfully big and I don't use the air fryer function. So I'm really interested in whether this new model can do what I need it to do without needing what looks like a very large Darth Vader helmet on my countertop. So let's see what this MultiPot XL can do.
What kinds of cooking does the Ninja MultiPot XL do?
The 11 different cooking functions of the Ninja MultiPot XL are:
- Slow cook
- Sear / sauté
- Bake
- Sauce
- Rice
- Pasta
- Mixed Rice
- Sous Vide
- Simmer
- Hotpot
- Keep warm

You'll notice the absence of air frying here, but that's definitely not a deal-breaker for me. It's one of the reasons this Ninja is so much smaller than my Foodi XL despite having almost the same maximum capacity.

Looking at what I usually cook, I reckon this could easily replace my Foodi Max. I typically use mine to sear or brown meat before slow cooking it, to sauté veg before adding stock for soup, and to make pasta. The keep warm feature is something I'm used to with the Foodi Max and I use it all the time, and the presence of a sous vide option is really attractive: I've tried stand-alone sous vide gadgets before and found them too much of a fuss but I'd be tempted to experiment with sous vide salmon and steaks here.

According to Ninja the pots are oven-safe up to 428F / 220C, they're dishwasher safe (as are the lids) and they can be nested for easy storage. The glass lids are a nice touch — I can't see what i'm cooking when I close the lid of my Foodi Max — and the small size makes this really tempting to me. It's small enough to carry over to the table, too.

There are only two obvious downsides to me. The first is the lack of pressure cooking, which is something I like to use from to time, and the second is that it will almost certainly have the infamous Ninja beep alert that all my Ninjas make. But those are minor issues. If you're big on cooking ideas but short of space this looks like it could be an excellent kitchen companion.
The Ninja MultiPot XL is available now direct from SharkNinja and major retailers. The list price is £259.99 (about $350 / AU$490).

articles.headline: Trump visits to safe red districts are a ‘considered strategy’ to fire up low-propensity voters: Byron York
keyFacts: Byron York said Donald Trump’s strategy of visiting deep red districts aims to energize low-propensity voters for midterm elections.
York noted that while Trump's presence boosts turnout for both parties, mobilizing these voters helps statewide Republican candidates.
Trump is traveling to Ohio on Wednesday to support Senator Jon Husted and gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy.
body: Washington Examiner chief political correspondent Byron York said President Donald Trump’s campaign strategy in deep red districts is to energize “low-propensity voters .”
“[Midterm elections] are normally sleepy, but the one thing we do know is that President Trump has a tremendous power to fire up people,” York said Tuesday on The Hugh Hewitt Show .
On the downside, York said Trump’s presence increases voter turnout for both Republicans and Democrats.
“If both of those, you know, powers are in effect this time, you could see some pretty serious turnout,” York said.

Last Thursday, York traveled with Trump to Sioux City, Iowa, a congressional district the president won by 31 points in 2024. While critics mocked the president for visiting deep red areas instead of swing districts, York said the chairman of the Republican party said it was about appealing to “low-propensity voters.”

“So when Trump says, ‘Please pretend like I’m on the ballot,’ and Democrats scoff at that, that’s actually a considered strategy,” York said. “Because if those voters actually do vote like Trump is on the ballot, then he’ll probably do better because when he won by 31 [points], that helped statewide Republican candidates win all across Iowa.”

Trump is going back to Ohio Wednesday to help out Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) in his race. Meanwhile, he’s also supporting the Republican Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy through his latest controversy involving an attack ad featuring his opponent’s estranged mother.

Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, was featured in an ad calling her daughter a liar. The ad was hit with backlash , bringing up Acton’s history of a traumatic childhood involving her stepfather’s alleged sexual abuse when she was young. Instead of retracting the ad, Ramaswamy embraced it, investing $4 million into promotion.
OBAMA RIPS RAMASWAMY AFTER ACTON AD: ‘NO OFFICE IS WORTH STOPPING THAT LOW’
York said Trump went out in “full support” of the ad despite Republicans , including Husted, “running from it.”

“My experience just watching Ramaswamy in the presidential race in [2024] is that he could, he really had the power to alienate people fairly quickly,” York said. “He could impress the heck out of somebody, and then, by about half an hour later, maybe, he was wearing a little thin on them.”

articles.headline: Raiders told to bench $341m star and start Fernando Mendoza against ‘trainwreck’ Jets
keyFacts: TalkSPORT podcasters Brian T. Smith and Jay Lawrence debated whether the Las Vegas Raiders should bench veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins for rookie Fernando Mendoza.
Smith argued that Mendoza should start against the New York Jets this weekend, while Lawrence suggested waiting until later in the season.
The Raiders currently sit on a four-game losing streak after starting the 2026 NFL season with three consecutive wins.
body: Fernando Mendoza’s time could be imminent.

The Las Vegas Raiders have not rushed the rookie quarterback into the starting lineup, with head coach Klint Kubiak instead opting to have him serve as a backup to veteran Kirk Cousins through the early weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
Mendoza is currently learning the NFL from the sideline, though he has now made his regular season debut Getty

After an emphatic start to the new campaign, where they started 3-0, and Cousins, who has made $314.4 million during his career, looked to have rolled back the years, the Raiders now find themselves on a four-game skid.
Their most recent loss came in a 35-21 defeat to the Los Angeles Rams , despite the 38-year-old signal caller throwing for 295 yards and two touchdowns.
With the 2-5 New York Jets next up on the schedule, an argument has been made that this could be the best time to deploy Mendoza under center for his first career NFL start.
Could Mendoza get his first NFL start against the Jets?

talkSPORT’s Brian T. Smith and Jay Lawrence were debating this exact topic during the latest episode of the Inside the NFL podcast, with Smith of the belief that Kubiak should consider making a change at quarterback, even if only temporarily.

“ Mendoza was a lock at number one . He was like Caleb Williams . He was like Trevor Lawrence . Perfect in Indiana, 16-0 the dream story ,” Smith said. “He was never going anywhere else besides the number one overall pick.
“So, the second he signs that contract, the second he’s drafted, then if you’re a fan, if you’re in the NFL media, if you’re a GM for another team, your whole focus shifts to when will he play?
“That’s all it’s about for the whole organization because that’s the green light. Then you’re taking the switch and you were flipping it and it all gets real at that point.”

Smith further argued that the Raiders’ current roster construction is not good enough to realistically compete for a playoff spot, let alone for the Super Bowl , and placed some of the blame on that on “hands-on” minority owner Tom Brady .

“The flip side is they’re playing the New York Jets this weekend and the Jets are an absolute train wreck …” Smith further argued. “What better scenario to you need the win, you can move to 4-4, you let Fernando Mendoza play.

“He’s in New York, but he’s not playing against the Giants, he’s not playing against a good team, he’s playing against the Jets. He’ll have 10,000 empty seats there. You’re going against Geno Smith . He’s a better quarterback walking the field.
The Raiders have already matched last season’s win total (3) with a .500 record to begin 2026 Getty
The Raiders opted to have Mendoza sit behind veteran Kirk Cousins as he acclimatizes to the NFL Getty

“Here is the problem after that. If he does not start against the Jets, I was just looking at this look at their schedule. They’re playing the Chiefs, they’re playing the Seahawks, they’re playing the Broncos. … But once he starts, you don’t take him off the field.”

Of course, Mendoza has already made his NFL debut, coming onto the field for a fourth-quarter cameo in the 45-17 blowout defeat to the New England Patriots in Week 5, where he completed six of eight passes for 48 yards, earning three first-downs.
Making a QB switch won’t address the concerns on offense

But for Lawrence, benching a 15-year veteran in Cousins this early in the season for an inexperienced rookie doesn’t make much sense, especially when the Raiders rushing attack – spearheaded by former first-round pick Ashton Jeanty (106 carries for 328 rushing yards and one touchdown) has struggled to get going.

“ Let’s not pretend that the only issue with this team or this offense is Kirk Cousins . That’s not the case,” Lawrence argued. “I would love for something to happen in the running game. I’d love for Ashton Jeanty to be this sure-fire hit running back.

“If you take Kirk Cousins out of the situation and you put Fernando Mendoza in this in the situation next week and you’ve got the same offense but with Mendoza running it, suddenly you’re not getting the wins, the fans aren’t happy with the situation, and there’s a lot of dour mood in Las Vegas later on this year.
“Or you can wait maybe until the off-season. But then again, I am coming at it from knowing that they’re not going to win the Super Bowl. … But they will always be attempting to do that. …
Mendoza has had his first taste of NFL action, but whether he will be given the opportunity to take center stage from the start at some point in 2026 remains to be seen Getty

“My ideal situation for him is Week 14 or 15,” Lawrence continued. “He gets to play those last three or four games. It doesn’t matter. He could be bad. It doesn’t matter because the whole season is over.

With a tough schedule coming up, in which they face four teams currently over .500 in their next five outings, the Week 8 clash against the Jets could be the best opportunity for the Raiders to really examine the talent they have in the Heisman Trophy winner .

“Fernando Mendoza has incredible confidence, incredible self-belief. He’s got crazy LinkedIn perseverance. I like everything about him. … But he’s going to have to play at some point,” Smith further argued.
“Like you either have it or you don’t. Caleb Williams played early. Drake Maye played early. Zach Wilson did too, and we saw how that that turned out.

“But Fernando Mendoza, if he plays midway through the season, and he faces some adversity, and he builds up his confidence, and he starts to understand the field, and things start to slow down, then he’s ready to go week one next year.
“I would put him in this week against the New York Jets.”

articles.headline: Yankees $313.5 million trade idea with Giants makes no sense for 2 reasons
keyFacts: Analyst Zachary D. Rymer proposed a trade where the New York Yankees acquire Rafael Devers from the San Francisco Giants.
The proposed deal would send right-handers Luis Gil and Carlo Lagrange to the Giants in exchange for Devers.
The trade idea is considered impractical because the Yankees already have numerous designated hitters and first basemen on their roster.
body: The New York Yankees don't need any more first basemen or designated hitters on their roster.
They may have too many already.
Ben Rice, Luis Garcia Jr., Giancarlo Stanton, and Aaron Judge are all hitters who could spend time at DH in 2027.
That's why Zachary D. Rymer's trade idea to acquire Rafael Devers from the San Francisco Giants makes little to no sense.
In Rymer's deal, the Yankees send right-handers Luis Gil and Carlo Lagrange to the Giants in exchange for Devers, a three-time All-Star who hit 37 home runs last season.
"These are all fair questions, but to hell with them anyway. At the least, it feels like the end of the line for Stanton in New York.

"And if so, the fit makes more sense. Devers has always hit at Yankee Stadium as if he belongs there, with his 18 home runs in New York representing the most for any stadium that he's never called home," Rymer wrote.
In this scenario, Stanton would've probably already been traded or released by the Yankees, and Garcia would be forced to move to another middle infield spot.
Rice would play first base, and Judge would play right field despite injury concerns.
Another reason why the Yankees might turn a cold shoulder to the idea of Devers? The long-term extension he signed with the Boston Red Sox.
San Francisco still owes the 30-year-old over $200 million through the 2033 season, when he will be 36 and almost certainly in the final stages of his career.
Devers is a talented hitter, but the Yankees don't need any more DH types clogging up the lineup, even without Stanton on the roster.

articles.headline: PlayStation Officially Reveals Gorgeous New ‘Prism’ PS5 Hardware
keyFacts: Sony Interactive Entertainment unveiled the Prism Collection on Wednesday, featuring transparent DualSense controllers and matching console covers in three colors.
The accessories will cost $84.99 for controllers and $74.99 for console covers, with pre-orders beginning on November 10 and the launch scheduled for February 4, 2027.
The collection arrives as Sony faces hardware questions, including a reported 2028 or 2029 release for the PlayStation 6 and plans to end physical game disc production in January 2028.
body: Sony Interactive Entertainment unveiled its new Prism Collection on Wednesday, a new line of PlayStation 5 accessories featuring transparent designs for DualSense controllers and matching console covers. The collection includes three color options: Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray.

Each design features a glossy, translucent exterior that offers a look at some of the hardware underneath. The collection also brings back the see-through aesthetic popular among electronics in the late 1990s, giving Sony's current-generation hardware a retro-inspired makeover.

The new DualSense controllers will cost $84.99 each in the U.S., while matching PS5 console covers will sell for $74.99. Both products feature the same three color options, allowing players to coordinate their controllers and consoles.

Pre-orders open Nov. 10 at 7 a.m. PT / 10 a.m. ET in the U.S. through PlayStation Direct and participating retailers. The Prism Collection launches Feb. 4, 2027, though availability and release dates may vary by region. The console covers will be sold directly through PlayStation in select countries, including the U.S., with limited quantities available through other retailers in some markets.
The future of PlayStation

The Prism Collection arrives as Sony faces questions about the future of its hardware, including the eventual PlayStation 6. Although Sony has not announced a release date, reports suggest the next console could arrive in 2028 or 2029, with rising memory costs potentially pushing its price toward $1,000.

Physical media is another point of contention. Sony has announced plans to end production of physical PlayStation game discs in January 2028, raising questions about whether the PS6 will include a disc drive. An optional external drive remains a possibility, but Sony has yet to confirm its plans.
For now, the Prism Collection offers PS5 owners a cosmetic upgrade rather than a new hardware generation.

body: Before HUNTR/X of K-Pop Demon Hunters fame, there was K/DA.

League of Legends’ first foray into the world of K-pop and music took over the airwaves and gaming community for the first time back in 2018 with its song “POP/STARS,” featuring characters from the game voiced by real-life musicians with legitimate songs as its own virtual K-pop group many years before Netflix’s trio become a phenomenon.

And now in 2026, the four member group is back once again with the same awesome and upbeat sound, but some fresh new voices on the tracks, including 22-year-old hyperpop singer Sophie Powers as Evelynn . She’s set to perform with Soyeon and Miyeon of i-dle, and fellow newcomer Mimi Webb at League’s Worlds tournament Grand Finals next month in Brooklyn, New York.

Image via Riot Games I spoke with Sophie on a video call recently and we chatted about the K/DA’s four track EP comeback including the viral “Firestarter” song that just debuted at the top of Spotify’s US and global charts, the upcoming live performance at Worlds, becoming Evelynn after other star singers like Madison Beer and Kim Petras portrayed her, and her own K-pop fandoms and background.
DESTRUCTOID: So, how’s this last week been for you? Not busy at all, huh?

SOPHIE POWERS: Really crazy. I am overwhelmed for sure, but definitely thankful. I’m really happy people are liking the songs. Even outside of Firestarter, like the B-sides, Watch Me , Girls , and Never Going Back. I’m only on Watch Me and Girls , but seeing the reception of those, it’s kind of like, you never know. And I got my nails done, K/DA themed, so that’s how good things are going.
(you can see her awesome nails below, she was very excited to show them off)
Screenshot by Destructoid How long have you known about this project? How did it all come about? Did you audition or was there an offer?

So, actually last year, it’s funny, I’m such a fan of (Netflix series) Arcane, which is obviously a part of the League of Legends and Riot Games franchise. It’s such a massive show, I’ve cosplayed Jinx a few times. And they had an Arcane Grammys event. And my friend Ryan, Royal & the Serpent, was performing. And my manager was there as well, so I went with my friend. And I met someone, I think I met the head of music at Riot. And we started talking, and I was telling him about how viral my American Idol thing went in Asia . And my collaboration with this girl group there named ILLIT. And obviously Asia is a really big part of League of Legends , that’s one of their biggest markets.

So, he was like, “we should get you to do something for Riot.” So, I wrote a bunch of songs, and they took none of them. But instead they were like, “we actually think that you would fit K/DA.” And I was like, “me!?” And they were like, “yeah, we’ve heard your voice, but we’re still going to have you audition,” right? And then I had to sing the songs. There were 15 different versions of each song, because there would be lyric tweaks, or songs that they liked and then they didn’t end up using. So, overall, it was a long process, but that’s kind of how it came to be.
What was it like watching the leaks begin flying around? (The song was actually released earlier than scheduled because of it)

I just remember seeing one leak posted, I think it was by some prediction market, Polymarket or something. And they said, ‘just announced Megan Thee Stallion rumored to be the next Evelynn.’ And I was like, ‘damn, I’m so cooked. Megan Thee Stallion. The people are going to be so disappointed when they realize.’ But thankfully, it was well received. And I’m superstitious. So I don’t believe anything is actually happening until I’ve signed the contract. Even if I’ve done the songs, even if I’ve done the interviews, filmed the content, etc. I’m like, ‘I haven’t signed that piece of paper, so this could be pulled under the rugs.’ It’s happened so many times before, I’m sure you know, entertainment industry. But it ended up happening.

‘ Firestarter’ is my first introduction to you, and this is likely to be the case for many mainstream fans. How would you describe yourself as a singer, songwriter, artist? What’s your elevator pitch to people discovering you for the first time?

My elevator pitch for me as an artist is “self-expression at its fullest.” My only goal is to encourage others to express themselves a little bit more, which is why I almost overexpress myself. Because if I can be up here, maybe that encourages someone else to just come up here a little bit, right? So, that’s kind of my goal with art. And I think, especially now, human art is more important than ever. Creativity is more important than ever. Mental health is more important than ever. That’s something else I’m super passionate about. And those are all topics and things that I keep in mind throughout all aspects of my art.

And I’m definitely a visual artist. Like, all my visuals, I direct almost everything. I creative direct everything. I creative direct for other artists. I write all my songs. I am so hands-on… everything you see is really me. And if you’re consuming that music, then, this sounds very parasocial, but, you know me. And I want my music to be that shoulder for you to lean on. That’s kind of, on a personal level, how I relate to my art, and how I want others to consume it with that in mind.
ya … ily @official_i_dle pic.twitter.com/dePeBFxrLq
— sophie powers (@sophiep0wers) October 20, 2026

As a fan of K-pop yourself, what does this collab mean to you to work with artists like Miyeon and Soyeon (of K-pop girl group i-dle, K/DA’s Ahri and Akali respectfully)? You brought receipts, posting footage of you at a concert of theirs a few years ago on social media, and now you’re working and performing with them.

It feels surreal. And it proves that, obviously overnight success is not a thing, but you never know what could happen. Like, truly. And I personally believe everything happens for a reason. I think there’s a reason I went to that concert and fell in love with i-dle and sort of attracted that energy. And that sounds very ‘woo-woo,’ but I just think that it was meant to be. I’ve been posting so much.

Because I’ve dreamt of this, you know? I’m actually such a League fan. All my friends are streamers and cosplayers. I grew up reading comic books and playing League with my brothers. It’s just kind of crazy to be a part of the community. And then all of a sudden you’re thrust into really a lot of eyes within the community, but also outside of it.
K/DA’s song ‘POP/STARS’ in 2018 was my first real intro to K-pop, along with many others in the West. How did you get into the genre, and who are some of your favorites and biases?

Blackpink was definitely my introduction to K-pop, and I kind of then, from there, got super into, funny enough, K/DA. And also Itzy and Red Velvet. And then I kind of transitioned into Stray Kids. And I would say that Stray Kids is my favorite K-pop group of all time now. And something crazy that happened for me with Stray Kids was they asked me to open their show with a DJ set in Toronto. Which is, they had me play a set outside of the venue right before their show in Toronto, which doesn’t happen. That just doesn’t happen in K-pop, right? They don’t do openers. So that was crazy.

And then, yeah, I got super into i-dle. And I would say that I don’t have, honestly, I don’t have biases in girl groups. Because I can never choose. Like, they’re all so beautiful and goddesses. But in boy groups, and Stray Kids, my bias would probably be Hyunjin or Bang Chan, I would say. But, yeah. They’re great. I got super into Blackpink in, like, 2019. And I feel like then K-pop started becoming super popular, and I would say, like, the pandemic. And then from then on, it’s just grown so much.
How did you prepare to become Evelynn for this latest iteration of K/DA? Did you do anything differently to step into the role?

A lot of it was stupid little things. I made sure to have super long nails whenever I was tracking for Evelynn. And I also made sure that I was rude to at least one man for an hour before. Like, very rude. Like, actually bullying them, low-key. And then after I kind of hit both of those markers, it was easy for me to embrace my femininity, you know? Kind of just doing my makeup, doing my hair, more like the physical aspects, I would say, helped me get into the mental. And then the vocals were just super easy from there.

‘Firestarter’ I loved right off the bat, but I also really enjoy ‘Watch Me’ and some of its fun lyrics, like “Hurricane when the forecast K/DA, there’s a hundred percent chance of slay.” What’s your favorite lyric out of the songs on the EP?

Definitely the opening verse of Watch Me , if I had to choose. ‘The Louvre gonna hang it.’ Like, body so tea that the Louvre is literally gonna hang that shit. Like, that is such a bar to me. And I just got to be in my Evelynn bag right off the bat, which was super cool.
How are preparations for the K/DA performance at Worlds going? Is there anything you can say about what to expect? No spoilers , but you recently posted a video of you dancing along to the song.

I will say the choreography for the show is going to be much more than just that. That TikTok doesn’t really accurately represent the show choreography, which makes sense. Like, you’re on a stage, it’s very different than what is needed for a music video for a TikTok. But I’ve really been rehearsing the live stage performance versus on camera dancing., because you kind of have to do both, right? The show is live streamed. So that’s been something really interesting that I’ve been playing with. And I think something that’s really cool is that I can say we are going to be a part of a bigger show experience. I don’t want to get in trouble, but that’s kind of all I can say on that. I feel like people can put the pieces together, though. One thing I can say, though, is I’m not performing ‘Watch Me’ live. And everyone keeps commenting ‘can’t wait to see this live.’ And I just want to make it clear, guys, this isn’t going to be played live [at Worlds].
K-pop fans may know you already from your feature on ILLIT’s 2025 song “Jellyous,” but you also have songwriting credits for groups like IVE and NMIXX. How did you get into K-pop songwriting?

Yeah, it’s so funny. I have been writing the past, like, two years. I actually went to song camps in Korea. I had a manager that was connected in K-pop. And, you know, it was kind of from there, once I got any sort of notoriety of my own artist project, I noticed they were more receptive to the songs I’d already written. And the songs didn’t change. It was just more of a, ‘oh, Sophie’s kind of known here, does she want to just feature on a song rather than just write for our group’ kind of thing?

And I have a lot of songs on hold right now and other collabs that I don’t want to get too much into. But, yeah, it’s been super amazing because I’, a K-pop consumer first before I was a K-pop writer. I’ve been a songwriter forever. But, yeah, that ILLIT collab was really fun. I will say that I think that a lot of the K-pop fans will be surprised at some of the other collabs that I have in store for my EP, so I’m super excited about that.
Do you you have any other dream collabs, K-pop or otherwise?

Dream collab right now, probably either Horse Girl, I don’t know if you know Horse Girl, I think she’s so cool. Yeah, either Horse Girl or Yves, who is from the K-pop space, which is so interesting because her team reached out to me asking me to do a feature on one of her songs so long ago. And it never lines up because I had the ILLIT collab actually release around that time. But I would say Yves, and I also love Bibi. I saw her show, we’re friends. I love her so much. But, yeah, and then Stray Kids. I’m such a Stray Kids lover. But that’s obvious. That would be insane.

Evelynn has been portrayed by multiple artists in the past, including Madison Beer, Kim Petras, Bea Miller, even voice actor Mara Junot in-game. How has it been stepping into that role after the others? Did you feel pressure sort of filling in those shoes?

I mean, I wanted to create new shoes. I don’t want to fill anyone’s shoes. And I wanted people to be open to the idea, obviously, and that in itself is pressure of, kind of winning people over, allowing the fans or consumers to see your vision of the character versus what they may have seen in the past. And I feel like that was truly my struggle. But I’m proud of myself. And I hope that I did right, you know, by Evelynn and by the other amazing singers who portrayed her in the past.
Gamers, like K-pop fans, can be notoriously loud and opinionated, and sometimes mean. How has the reception to your inclusion in this K/DA iteration been?

Well, at first, I was really letting the hate get to me because I’ve experienced a lot of hate before. I’ve gone viral on social media. Being an artist, not everyone’s going to love you. And you have to understand that. But obviously, you still want people to love your art or, you know, what you poured your heart and soul into. So, seeing some of that hate was obviously disheartening. But I’ve also received so much love. And I just feel like this sounds so cheesy, but love truly does always win. And once you just don’t look at the hate and you only look at the positives, I mean I haven’t really seen a lot of hate since I just started interacting with the love. I don’t know if my algorithm changed.

But, yeah, I’ve been super thankful and overwhelmed with it since I started opening my eyes. And I hope that, you know, any hate that I did receive or am still receiving, people are just coming at it from the place of, they are nostalgic and they see the character a different way than I do. But it’s not that they vehemently just hate me as a person. Like, that’d be unfortunate. But I feel like that’s why I’m okay with it. I understand. Obviously, those characters, like Evelynn, they knew her. They knew other singers who portrayed her before they knew me, so, it makes sense.
The interview has been edited for brevity and accuracy.
The post K/DA Q&A: Sophie Powers, new voice of Evelynn, talks ‘Firestarter’ EP, her K-pop biases, and League of Legends Worlds performance appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: No clear winner in Israeli election as polls suggest stalemate
keyFacts: Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor the opposition bloc secured a majority in Israel's election, official vote counts show.
Opposition leader Yair Golan urged allies to partner with Arab parties to unseat Netanyahu, but Netanyahu rejected working with Arab parties.
If neither bloc builds a majority coalition, Israel could form a minority government, create a unity government, or hold new elections.
body: No clear winner emerged in Israel's elections on Wednesday with the vote count still under way. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor the opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, secured a majority, according to exit polls on Tuesday night.
With 85% of votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud party has 20.8% and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1%, according to official election data.

Local media projected 53 seats for Likud and allied parties, 48 for Yashar and allied parties and 19 for Arab-led parties. Each would need 61 seats for a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, in order to form a government.
On Wednesday morning, the head of Israel's main left-wing party called for his opposition allies to work with Arab parties to unseat Netanyahu.

"We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," Yair Golan said on X. "We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens."
Netanyahu dismissed the idea of partnership with Arab parties, instead calling on his allies to form a "right-wing, nationalist government."
"We must not endanger Israel and establish a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties," Netanyahu said on Wednesday morning.

Israel's two Arab parties won more seats in parliament than in any previous election. That electoral success comes after what some Arab voters told CBS News was a difficult time for them in the country under the hard-right government of Netanyahu, prompting a historic turnout for the minority community.

Both Netanyahu and those opposing him have previously vowed not to form a government reliant on Arab parties, arguing it would endanger the country if they gain enough seats to influence Israel's engagement in its myriad conflicts. Arab citizens of Israel are around 20% of the population.

If the opposition breaks their pre-election vow — a common occurrence in Israeli politics — they could take power and remove Netanyahu. A central tenet of Netanyahu's election campaign was keeping the Arab parties out of power.

Another possibility given the current stalemate, analysts say, is a unity government between the pro-Netanyahu and opposition blocs without the Arab parties or the ultra-Orthodox. The question in this scenario is who would be prime minister or whether Eizenkot or Netanyahu could rotate out of the position.

This is the first election since the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas, which authorities have acknowledged as since the country's founding in 1948. Israelis headed to the polls with their country still fighting in the subsequent multifront war in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and after two direct rounds of conflict with Iran and .
For many Israelis, after three years of war on multiple fronts, the election is seen as existential, and voter turnout appeared to be high.
Netanyahu vs. the "change bloc"

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister and leader of the Likud party, is seeking to form another coalition similar to his current government, which relies on partnerships with ultranationalist and Jewish religious parties.
Netanyahu is telling voters that Israel's campaigns in Gaza, Lebanon and especially Iran, are ongoing, and he needs more time to finish what his government started.

President Trump offered a full-throated last week. He reiterated his administration's firm support for the war the two men launched jointly against Iran almost eight months ago, and warned that he could be disinclined to continue with it if Netanyahu doesn't hold onto power.
"If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social.
Running against Netanyahu is a diverse group of parties with different ideologies but one clear common denominator: They all want Netanyahu out of power.

The front-runner to lead the "change bloc," should its various parties collectively win enough seats to build a coalition, is former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party.

"The Israeli public has voted against Netanyahu's service as Israel's prime minister," Eisenkot said in a rally late Tuesday, according to Reuters. "A worthy leader would have accepted the people's non-confidence and announced today his retirement from politics."

Eisenkot lost his son and two nephews while they were serving in the military in Gaza. He was part of the Israeli war cabinet for much of the first year of the Gaza war, working alongside Netanyahu. About half of his party's candidates in Tuesday's election are women, in stark contrast to the male-dominated Netanyahu coalition.
Eisenkot is framing himself as a humble veteran who wants to reunite Israel after years of division that he blames on Netanyahu.
What happens next?
In the event that neither bloc wins a clear majority in the Knesset, there are several paths forward to a new Israeli government.

One option is that parties or individual lawmakers could break election promises and switch sides, for which there is plenty of precedent in Israeli politics. There could be weeks of negotiating before a coalition is agreed on.

Another possibility is the change bloc, if it wins a significant share of the votes but not quite a majority, could seek to form a minority government. To do that, the parties just need to win more seats collectively than the other side, even if it's not more than the 50% of the 120 available.
Arab parties could give the change bloc that plurality by either voting in favor of a minority government, or just abstaining and not voting against its formation.
If there's a stalemate and neither side can build a coalition government, the country will have to hold new elections. There is plenty of precedent for that scenario, too.
Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five elections due to electoral deadlock.

articles.headline: The leader FEMA couldn’t keep
keyFacts: Former FEMA leader David Richardson arrived at the agency weeks before a July 2025 flood to reform its operations.
Whistleblowers and former officials said Richardson took swift action against waste and bureaucracy based on congressional mandates.
Richardson resigned after refusing to continue working for Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.
body: We didn’t work for David Richardson , but we knew him. We are part of a team of seven former senior executives and military officers who blew the whistle on waste, fraud, and retaliation in the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Puerto Rico recovery. For seven years, we worked through the agency’s bureaucracy, and it produced delays. We called it the “Great Circle of Unaccountability”: its real mission is preserving jobs and obfuscating. Disaster recovery is a side hustle.

Then we got a half hour with Richardson. More moved in the days after that meeting than in the seven years before it. When his book, Texas Flood 4 July 2025 : Power, Money, Politics, History, Bureaucracy, and Tragedy , came out, we contacted him because the leader on the page is the leader we met.

Richardson arrived at FEMA weeks before the July 4, 2025, flood on the Guadalupe River, sent, as he puts it, to “shut it down or reform it” with hurricane season bearing down. The book weaves the Texas response, a history of American floods, and Homeland Security politics into one argument: “During a crisis, good leaders go to the greatest point of friction, whether or not it costs them their life, reputation, or job.”
DAVID RICHARDSON: I RAN FEMA. HERE’S WHY YOU’RE PAYING FOR RICH PEOPLE TO LIVE ON THE BEACH

The flood history alone is worth the price. From Johnstown, where a neglected dam’s leaks were plugged “with mud and straw,” to Rapid City, where the sirens never sounded, the lesson repeats: the water is not the only cause of death.

He writes as he leads: bluntly, with wry humor. On his second day, he spent 90 minutes with senior staff until they agreed on a one-sentence problem statement: “FEMA does not know the Administration’s intent for the 2025 hurricane season.” Then he promised a hurricane strategy in two weeks. One member of the team that wrote it remembers the cost: “There was a team of us that spent like 15 days working with him, 15 days straight … even on weekends with him.” Then-DHS Secretary Kristi Noem refused to approve it.

So much for his widely reported remark that he didn’t know the United States had a hurricane season. “He obviously knew the date,” the same team member said. A senior political appointee at FEMA told us Richardson “was chagrined that Noem didn’t sign off on the Hurricane Strategy … because it was forward leaning and ahead of the FEMA Review Council,” so he asked, in irony aimed at her, “Who knew there was a hurricane season coming?”

“It wasn’t a joke,” the appointee said. “He was in disbelief Noem would do something so stupid.” FEMA staff, the appointee added, knew he was serious about reform and ran to the press with the remark, knowing it would be taken out of context.

When the flood came, the point of friction was in Washington : a memo requiring Noem herself to sign every contract over $100,000. Noem flew to Texas with an entourage; Richardson stayed back to fight the memo, kept his footprint small, and shut out hangers-on. With search-and-rescue teams waiting, he overrode Noem’s memo and sent them when DHS headquarters dragged its feet. Anthony Antognoli, who served at his side, explains why critics called Richardson unreachable: “He was always available and connected to those who mattered and were working to respond to the tragedy; he was too focused to respond to those who were unequipped or unwilling to get help to Texas.”

The book’s spine is a mission analysis. Richardson’s team pulled the roughly 35 laws governing FEMA, extracted about 150 tasks Congress requires, and distilled them into eight mission-essential tasks. FEMA’s mission statement, “Help people before, during, and after a disaster,” he notes, “encourages mission creep and sounds good. That’s it.” The result: FEMA grew from no more than 4,000 personnel in 2006 to 25,000 positions today, adding an office for compensation for lost heirlooms and an army of 300 lawyers.

A former senior FEMA official who worked alongside him agrees: “This is the exact work that we have done when we arrived at FEMA, which is the mission analysis, looking at existing laws and aligning the organization based on that analysis.” Of Richardson, the official said, “His leadership style is very direct. There is no ambiguity.”

To Richardson, a Marine , an agency’s mission is dictated by law, not good intentions. Our team knew his approach intimately: several members were decorated former combat officers, and all of us had worked with the Marines as consultants. We did something similar in Puerto Rico: mapped the mission to tasks and cut the rest. Applied to FEMA, his approach would have shrunk and focused the agency — serving survivors and taxpayers, but not the people who run it.

The closing section, “Things Americans Should Know,” holds the book’s sharpest analysis. Richardson sorts the causes of the Texas deaths into immediate, proximate, and deep, and names the deep cause: building in the floodplain, fostered by federal flood insurance and mapping programs. That is root-cause analysis, our own discipline.

He proposes replacing years of site-by-site damage inspections with block grants based on “parametric models leveraging aerial photography and other techniques” to cut fraud and field staff. “Few want this,” he adds. We can confirm. In Puerto Rico, a digital site inspection tool that would have saved FEMA an estimated $70 million and shaved years off the recovery was lost.

He describes more than 80,000 open public assistance projects, some dating back to Hurricane Katrina, producing “an endless chain of extended deadlines, disputed claims, and finger-pointing where nobody is held accountable for the prudent close-out of projects.” That is the Great Circle of Unaccountability at work, and it should surprise no one. The lack of accountability runs through DHS in general, and FEMA in particular, and even the department’s watchdog reflects it. From fiscal 2019-2025, the DHS Inspector General acted on just 1,070 of 140,344 waste, fraud, and abuse complaints, or 0.76%; peer agencies act on 2% to 10%. Whistleblowers fared worse: only 11 of 3,144 retaliation complaints, or 0.35%, were validated, against 3% to 8% at other federal watchdogs.

We met with Richardson a few months after he arrived at FEMA. He took nothing on faith; he grilled us with pointed questions, had his staff pull the records and verify our claims, reviewed what came back, and, within days, acted decisively against the malfeasance and bad actors we had identified. He did not shoot from the hip or bury it in a working group. He lived what he writes in his book: “Decisive and justifiable action is the hallmark of a leader.”

To our team, Richardson was a breath of fresh air: the first official to give us real hope of resolving not just our issues but FEMA’s problems writ large. To FEMA, his directness, decisiveness, and competence made him a threat.
DAVID RICHARDSON: HOW ONE WORD BUILT FEMA’S BILLION-DOLLAR GRAVY TRAIN

Richardson stayed through hurricane season, as promised, “nursing a morbidly obese patient of an agency,” then resigned. What the book leaves out, he told us, is that he refused to keep working for Noem. His verdict on reform could serve as his FEMA epitaph: leaders able to carry it out “are nowhere to be found. The intestinal fortitude combined with the know-how is simply lacking.” For a few months, FEMA had both. Survivors, taxpayers, and whistleblowers like us lost the one leader who actually led.
Read this book as a field manual for leadership in government.

Barry Angeline is a retired executive with more than 30 years of experience leading process improvement at General Electric, Sun Microsystems, Time Warner, the Marine Corps, and the Army. He led FEMA’s Lean Six Sigma deployment in Puerto Rico.
Retired Col. Dan McCabe, U.S. Army, earned two Bronze Stars as an armor officer during Operation Iraqi Freedom and served as a senior consultant on FEMA’s Lean Six Sigma mission in Puerto Rico.

articles.headline: 8BitDo’s new Xbox Elite-style controller sets a high bar for customization
keyFacts: 8BitDo released the Ultimate 3E, a 150 dollar Xbox and PC controller designed for high-level customization.
The reviewer stated that the controller features modular buttons, drift-proof TMR joysticks, and a wireless charging dock.
The reviewer noted that despite its extensive features, the high price makes it difficult to recommend over cheaper alternatives.
body: It’s hard to make an Xbox controller that stands out these days, especially one that’s expensive, due to a wealth of great semi-affordable options. Still, 8BitDo’s $150 Ultimate 3E is a bold controller that holds its own against other feature-packed options. It’s made for Xbox and PC gamers who want a deeper level of customization and a more refined design than Microsoft’s pricier Xbox Elite Series 2 and 8BitDo’s own $60 Ultimate 2.
8BitDo’s new Xbox Elite-style controller sets a high bar for customization
The retro controller maker’s first real swing at a premium controller feels great, but it doesn’t earn its high price tag.

Basically every feature I’m looking for in a controller is here, plus some, including drift-proof TMR joysticks, extra shoulder buttons, rear paddles, motion control support, modular buttons and joysticks, a 3.5mm jack for chat or private listening, and a 1,000Hz polling rate over a low-latency wireless connection (only when connected to a PC). It includes a carrying case and a wireless charging dock that you can stash the USB dongle within.

8BitDo’s first premium controller is in direct competition with other big names, like Razer, PowerA, SteelSeries, as well as rising star GameSir. But the Ultimate 3E is also among the most expensive of the bunch, and I’m not sure the company delivers enough additional features to pull it off.

The Ultimate 3E’s modular design opens up more customization than a lot of other controllers I’ve tried. It includes two four-button modules (one with membrane buttons, and another with clickier microswitch buttons), two directional pads, and three extra joysticks. That level of customization and included accessories should hopefully help it age more gracefully than cheaper alternatives.

Its TMR joystick mechanisms shouldn’t wear down, so you’ll only need to be concerned with replacing the joystick tops down the line, and the controller includes several to choose from. However, 8BitDo doesn’t sell replacement accessories for the Ultimate 3E, as it does for many of its other controllers, and it hasn’t responded to The Verge as to whether it ever will.

The Ultimate 3E’s modularity also helps somewhat to make up for the high price tag. 8BitDo’s Pro 3 already lets you swap individual magnetically attaching buttons to accommodate different console layouts. The Ultimate 3E doesn’t offer as much freedom of per-button placement as the Pro 3, likely due to being intended for use with Xbox and PC, but the joy of using its microswitch button module makes up for the limitation. They’re sharp and clicky, although they have a bit more travel than I’d like.

My other complaints are relatively minor. The clips that hold the face button module in place are very tight, and I found myself having to carefully use a plastic toothpick to pop them out. Similarly, swapping out joysticks requires a surprising amount of force, and I had to work up the courage to yank them off the first time. And, even when set to their higher response point, the triggers feel a bit soft, and, like the membrane buttons, have more travel than I prefer, although the extra shoulder button can offset that travel distance in some situations. The soft touch grips and back gather dust and gunk pretty quickly, although you can at least clean the joystick tops by removing them.

It’s as weird of a time to be releasing a new high-end Xbox controller as it is shopping for one. Assuming you’re not content with the solid but basic Microsoft model that’s around $50, it seems unwise to commit to spending well over $100 on one given the increased frequency of Xbox Elite Series 3 leaks. What we’ve seen of that, while unofficial, seems interesting: it appears to not offer the modular customization of the Ultimate 3E, but its screen and knobs might be what some people want in their next controller.

As for how the Ultimate 3E stacks up to other great controllers, Microsoft’s Elite Series 2 is a poor value by comparison. It uses potentiometer joysticks that are likely to drift over time, which to me feels disqualifying given the price point. I don’t think anyone using 8BitDo’s Ultimate 2 should feel the urge to upgrade to the Ultimate 3E. There just aren’t enough differences to make it worthwhile. However, there’s also a non-modular 8BitDo Ultimate 3 for $99, which may end up being a sweet spot for more budget-conscious gamers who don’t need to tinker as much.

For what it’s worth, I’ll be sitting down with the GameSir G7 Pro to play GTA VI. It’s one of my favorite Xbox controllers, and has a nearly-identical set of features and specs to the 8BitDo. Better yet, it’s only $80 at full price, and comes in a variety of colors, with swappable faceplates for sale.

Overall, the Ultimate 3E feels similar to use as other Elite-style controllers I’ve tried, and that’s impressive for a company that hasn’t tried to take on pricier competition before. Whether you opt for the cheaper Ultimate 3 with mostly-similar specs, or the pricier, more customizable Ultimate 3E, 8BitDo’s high-end gamepads make a strong impression, but they’re tough to recommend when there are cheaper alternatives that don’t slack on features.

articles.headline: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
keyFacts: Nvidia released the free, open-weight Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe model and version 2 of its Granary speech dataset on Wednesday.
The tools target developers building business meeting and medical transcription apps to customize software for industry jargon, though Transcribe only works with recorded audio.
Nvidia stated the 30-billion-parameter model can run on a single chip across various devices while joining other recent AI voice releases from competitors.
body: Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open-source speech dataset.

Nvidia boasts that Nemotron 3.5 can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks, including Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard.

These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language. One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not live streams.

Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chip powering new laptops, to Blackwell datacenter chips. It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yet powerful Parakeet (1.1 billion parameters).

Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during busy period of AI voice releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce released Launa-Omni, its voice model.

keyFacts: Recalled England centre Joe Marchant said the RFU selection policy excluding players based abroad is tough to deal with.

body: Nations Championship: Joe Marchant says England's selection policy tough to deal with for players outside Prem

Joe Marchant chats to Sky Sports following return to England squad after signing for Sale in summer; Marchant was ineligible for England for three seasons 2023/24-2025/26 due to playing for Stade Francais in France's Top 14; Marchant says he wanted to play Test rugby the entire time
Wednesday 28 October 2026 15:11, UK
Recalled England centre Joe Marchant admits the RFU selection policy which prohibits players being selected from outside of the Prem is tough for players abroad to deal with.
For three seasons between 2023/24 and 2025/26, Marchant - who has 28 caps - was ineligible to represent England due to playing with Stade Francais in France's Top 14.
The 30-year-old returned to Prem Rugby with Sale Sharks over the summer, and has since been included in England's squad ahead of November's Nations Championship.
However, players like Jack Willis at Toulouse, Tom Willis at Bordeaux and Kyle Sinckler at Toulon still cannot be picked.
"The whole time I was there, I wanted to be back playing for England," Marchant told Sky Sports. "We obviously know the rules, but I just wanted to be back in an England shirt.
"It's a tough one, and obviously it's a big debate at the moment. But especially when I was there, I just wanted to be back in the England mixer.
"That's why, when the opportunity came to go to Sale, it was a good one for me at the time."

England have an upcoming three-day training camp ahead of their Nations Championship schedule, for which Steve Borthwick has named a 36-player squad who will gather at England's performance centre at Pennyhill Park.

England face Australia, Japan and New Zealand throughout November, in a series that represents their final opportunity to test themselves against southern hemisphere opposition before the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

For Marchant, he admits returning to the England fold has happened quicker than he imagined, while he now has hopes of forcing his way into Borthwick's England plans for the 2027 World Cup in Australia.

"I'm absolutely buzzing, it's been really good to be back into camp. All the boys have been great. It's been obviously a lot of new faces since I left, but I'm really enjoying being back in with the lads," he said.
"I was just hoping, to be honest. I was obviously coming back into England, and I wanted to put my best foot forward and see if I can get in the mixer.
"There's still some selection stuff to go, and hopefully I'll be in the mixer when it comes in a week's time.

"I think [I have] just a little bit more experience all round. The Top 14 is a very competitive league. There's lots of good athletes all around, and I think it's one of those where you learn the real intense moments to win and lose a game.
"Hopefully, I can bring a little bit of that back.
"I feel like a better player. I feel like I've gone there and now feel a bit refreshed. Obviously, there's a change of [England] set-up, change of environment. You've got to learn new things.
"As a kid, all I wanted to do was play for England, and I've been very lucky that I've been able to do it a few times. If I can do it again, that'd be awesome, and at a World Cup even better."

articles.headline: Sony Is Bringing The Best Trend Of ’90s Console Design To PS5
keyFacts: Sony announced the Prism Collection, featuring transparent DualSense controllers and PS5 console covers in Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray.
Sony designers Leo Cardoso and Satoshi Aoyagi stated the products were inspired by late '90s see-through hardware trends and modern industrial design.
Preorders begin on November 10 through PlayStation Direct, and the items will launch on February 4, 2027, with controllers priced at $85 and covers at $75.
body: Sony is embracing one of the best trends of the late '90s and early 2000s, revealing a new line of DualSense controllers and PlayStation 5 console covers with transparent materials. Dubbed the Prism Collection, it will come in three distinct glossy colors: Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray. Preorders will open on November 10 through the PlayStation Direct store ahead of a February 4, 2027 rollout.

Sony says the design was inspired by the PS5 design team's interest in giving the console and its accessories a transparent look while also showing off the hardware beneath the protective surface. Flare Orange has a "bold and vibrant aesthetic," Emerald Green offers an "elegant" finish, and Sony says a PS5 will look "refined" with a Graphite Gray cover.

"We know how much our fans have been looking forward to the return of transparent controllers," Leo Cardoso and Satoshi Aoyagi from Sony's Color, Material, and Finish design team said in a press statement. "We wanted to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late '90s in a fresh, modern way that complements the PS5's industrial design. "The high-gloss clear finish extends across the back of the controller, offering a look at the technology that powers the DualSense controller while maintaining a sleek, monochromatic look. The metallic finish on the middle cover brings the contrasting surfaces together for a premium appearance that feels consistent with the PS5 generation."

The Prism Collection DualSense controllers have an MSRP of $85 each, while the PS5 console covers are priced at $75 each. If you missed it, Sony also launched limited-edition Marathon and Gran Turismo DualSense controllers this year, and Marvel's Wolverine fans can grab a new PS5 console cover and matching DualSense controller in striking yellow or adamantium-inspired silver, complete with claw marks.

articles.headline: GOG's getting into publishing in its new, post-CD-Projekt life, and it already has games on the way
keyFacts: DRM-free storefront GOG has partnered with independent publisher Retrovibe to launch a new publishing initiative called Retrovibe by GOG.
The partnership was facilitated by GOG owner Michał Kiciński, who also co-founded Retrovibe.
The new initiative will release games including Cop Bastard and Project Warlock: Lost Chapters across multiple storefronts.
body: Cast your mind back to January and you might remember a sit-down we had with some of the leaders of a newly-independent GOG. The DRM-free storefront had separated from its former owner—CD Projekt—and returned to the arms of its original cofounder, Michał Kiciński. Back then, Kiciński told us that publishing was one of the several moves GOG was considering in its post-CDP life. Well, the day has finally come.

"Together with an independent publisher, Retrovibe, we’re joining forces to launch Retrovibe by GOG, a new initiative supporting independent developers in bringing their games to players across PC storefronts and consoles," reads the announcement press release.

The publisher will do, well, publisher stuff. Funding, marketing, hobnobbing with content creators and game journalists (an unenviable task), and getting games certified for release on all of the good Lord's wonderful platforms.

Why has GOG signed up with Retrovibe in particular? Well, there's an affinity between GOG's focus on releasing and preserving old games (good old games, you might say) and Retrovibe's focus on games that capture some sort of classic essence. But a big reason is that Retrovibe was also cofounded by Kiciński: in our January chat, he noted that he had a 50% stake in the publisher.

So it was probably a relatively easy marriage to make happen: "With GOG now under the ownership of its original co-founder, Michał Kiciński, who also co-founded Retrovibe, the two companies have an opportunity to work more closely together," says the announcement, touting Retrovibe's publishing nous and GOG's "platform expertise, marketing capabilities and connection to PC players worldwide."

The new publishing chimera already has a game under its stamp: Cop Bastard, which releases tomorrow, the 29th of October. It has a very good name and a sort of 'what if you equipped a John Woo protagonist with a bodycam' aesthetic. Our (formerly our) Robin Valentine wrote that there was "definitely something alluring about Cop Bastard's brand of deep-fried retro weirdness" when he tried it last year, though he feared it might not hold up over a full playthrough.

Also on the GOG/Retrovibe docket is Project Warlock: Lost Chapters, the third in the Project Warlock line of boomer shooters. It's not as good a name as Cop Bastard but it does have a great look to it..
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

You might notice that, despite officially being embraced into the GOG publishing bosom, both those games are not GOG-sclusives. They each have Steam pages as well as GOG releases, which I confess to being quite happy about, if for no other reason than GOG's Galaxy client doesn't yet have its promised Linux build.

One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War.
