articles.headline: Serious consequences Ilhan Omar could face as immigration probe is thrown into spotlight: judge
keyFacts: Rep. Ilhan Omar is the subject of two ongoing federal probes involving alleged immigration fraud and financial disclosures.
Attorney Nathan Hansen stated that a criminal conviction for a naturalized citizen does not automatically trigger denaturalization.
Investigators have seized Omar's phone, passport, computer, and DNA as part of the ongoing federal investigation.
body: There are two federal probes ongoing into the congresswoman — the first into alleged immigration fraud and the second involving her financial disclosures and a sharp discrepancy reported just one year apart.

“If somebody who’s a naturalized citizen — which I believe Ilhan Omar is — is convicted of a crime, that doesn’t automatically mean that they face denaturalization or anything like that,” Nathan Hansen, an attorney of 23 years, told Fox News Digital. “They would be handled by any type of other normal punishment that would come from the court.”
Hansen was appointed by former Attorney General Pam Bondi to serve as an immigration judge earlier this year. He served in the role for four months.

Denaturalization proceedings are separate from any criminal case that could arise from the federal investigation into Omar, whose “real name,” according to sources familiar with the investigation, is Ilhan Nur Said Elmi. Omar is under investigation for alleged immigration fraud related to the way she or her late father filled out her citizenship paperwork.

“A denaturalization proceeding, or somebody to strip somebody of their naturalization, is another proceeding, which would be a civil proceeding brought by the Department of Justice, presumably maybe on behalf of the Department for Homeland Security, who handles most of these things,” said Hansen.

“If there was some sort of nexus between the criminal conviction and somebody’s citizenship, it might be more likely that the Department of Justice would bring a denaturalization proceeding,” Hansen continued. “But I think it would be a discretionary matter within the people who are running the Justice Department.”
During the raid, investigators reportedly seized the congresswoman’s phone, passport, and computer. Fox News later confirmed that authorities are in possession of her DNA.

Regarding the case, observers have speculated that if indeed Omar has broken the law, statutes of limitations could hinder a prosecution. Hansen has seen those claims but doesn’t believe them to be valid.

“My view of that is generally that fraud stops any statute of limitations. In other words, if something isn’t disclosed or something’s hidden, then it would be unfair to the other party to toll a statute of limitations against them,” said Hansen. “That’s just sort of a general principle of law.”
Here’s the latest on the ongoing immigration investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar
Asked about the prevalence of immigration fraud in general, Hansen pointed to the sheer number of pending immigration and removal cases across the country and in Minnesota.

“I think I would take it from a 30,000-foot view of just the amount of cases that the United States is facing right now of people coming here,” he said. “It’s got to be in the tens of millions of people coming here, I think, but certainly millions.”
He said that in Minnesota alone, there are 20,000 to 30,000 removal cases pending that do not have a scheduled court date, due to a massive backlog of immigration-related cases.
“Whether you want to call it fraud or whatever, it’s like an overwhelming of the system and the system is not being used in the way in which it was intended,” he explained.
Bogus asylum claims are also contributing to the backlog, Hansen explained.

“Asylum relief has to do with protected grounds,” he said. “The most common ones are that, ‘I was persecuted at the acquiescence or directly at the behest at the government I am fleeing from based upon my race, my religion, my ethnicity [or] my political views.’ These are common claims.”
Hansen said that during the time when he was an immigration judge, he frequently saw claims that “just totally didn’t add up,” or documents provided by the applicant were “clearly fake.”

“There were other asylum applications that just clearly lacked merit under existing law,” he continued. “I mean, people would — I’ve seen cases where people would say, ‘Well, people insulted me in my country.’ And my response to that is, ‘Your country probably provides more protection against insults than the United States. In the United States, we have freedom of speech, and for the most part, you can be as rude as you want to someone and insult them, and it’s not a crime.'”

articles.headline: Valve addresses Steam's AI game cloning problem - by suggesting developers make their games less copyable
keyFacts: Valve business team members addressed concerns about AI-generated game cloning on Steam during a developer conference in Korea.
Valve representatives stated they do not want to act as gatekeepers and suggested developers make their games more complex to deter copycats.
Valve indicated that game ransoming issues are likely a matter for law enforcement rather than platform intervention.
body: Valve has responded to the worrying trend of games being cloned using generative-AI and sold on Steam, but instead of admonishing those games or promising to do something about them, it appears to have put the onus on developers to make their games less copyable.

Valve's business team members Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson were reportedly asked at a Steam Indie Connect developer conference in Korea, reported by InvenGlobal, whether Steam had any protective measures in place to stop games being cloned by AI. The questioner, a developer, cited an example whereby developers were held to ransom by people threatening to clone a game.

It was in response that example that Giardino - after saying this was the first he'd heard of ransoming, and that probably it was an issue for law enforcement, though Valve would "help in whatever way we can" - outlined not what Valve was doing to clamp down on this, but what developers could do to guard against it. Indeed, Giardino began by underlining Valve's hands-off stance towards AI use, reportedly stating: "We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use."

Instead, developers can guard against copycats by building active communities and establishing trust and by making a legitimate version of a game the best version available, Giardino reportedly said. Then there's the game itself: a more complex game will be harder to copy. "Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective," Giardino reportedly said.

It's worth remembering Valve's comments here come second-hand, and via machine translation which InvenGlobal has separately verified with a native Korean speaker; we're asking Valve for clarification. But they also come after the widely publicised case of Needle in a Haystack Simulator, a simple indie game which isn't even out yet, but has been copied so many times it's hard to know which game is the original. The game's developer has resorted to joking that they're implementing a new game mode where you have to find the original game amidst a pile of copycats.

Without Valve's intervention, it's hard to see what a developer can do to guard against this. How can you build a community and trust, and ensure your game is the best version available, if you're not given a chance at finding an audience to begin with?

Plus, the sheer number of copycats makes this a whack-a-mole situation for containment, which is something that - without Valve's help - probably requires expensive legal resources anyway, which in turn is probably out of reach for many indie developers. Also, legal reprimands usually don't occur until long after the damage has been done.

This wouldn't be the first time Valve has distanced itself from moderating what's sold on its PC platform. Indeed in 2018, amidst growing concern about the kinds of games available on Steam, Valve seemed to back away entirely from taking responsibility.

"We've decided that the right approach is to allow everything onto the Steam Store," Valve's Erik Johnson said at the time, "except for things that we decide are illegal, or straight up trolling." It's a stance that former Eurogamer editor Oli called "arrogant and cowardly".

More recently, the pendulum swung the other way when Valve threw an undiscerning net over an entire sector of 'adult' games, catching in it a slew of well-meaning, artistically mature games, as well as those of a more crass nature. And with Steam growing every year, and more games being released on the platform than ever before, the everpresent issue of moderation is certainly not going to disappear.

articles.headline: Amazon’s new Echo Dot can turn into a Wi-Fi extender – how it works
keyFacts: Amazon unveiled the new-generation Echo Dot devices featuring a built-in Eero Wi-Fi extender.
The new Echo Dots function as smart home hubs and are available to buy now for $100.
Amazon stated that the devices use an AI Accelerator for faster processing and better noise filtering.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Amazon unveiled the next-generation Echo Dot devices.
- The new Echo Dots serve as Wi-Fi extenders and smart home hubs.
- The devices are available to buy now for $100.

New Amazon Echo Dot devices have arrived, with a notable added feature: A built-in Eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 1,000 square feet of Wi-Fi coverage to your home network. On Wednesday, Amazon unveiled the Echo Dot along with several other new Alexa devices, including the Echo Show 16 smart home hub, the Echo Time smart alarm clock, and the Alexa Photo Frame.
A smart home hub

Amazon turned the new-generation Echo Dot into a smart home hub, with Alexa connecting to thousands of compatible devices like lights, locks, and thermostats out of the box, Amazon says. The device uses a sensor fusion platform to sense the room around it, and can detect things like a temperature drop and turn up the thermostat, or turn on the lights when you arrive home.

The Echo Dot features Amazon’s AZ3 silicon and a new AI Accelerator for on-device AI processing, for faster, more natural conversations with Alexa and better background noise filtering. A new fourth microphone helps Alexa hear you better no matter where you are in the room. Voice ID can also recognize who is speaking and customize your experience (for example, playing your favorite playlist instead of someone else’s in the home).
In terms of audio, the new Echo Dots include 50% more bass than the last model, according to Amazon.

These new Amazon smart home devices arrive just weeks after Apple unveiled its new smart home forays, including an Echo Show competitor called the Home View and the Echo Dot-like HomePod mini. But Amazon’s big advantage over Apple in the smart home is its current dominance: As of January, Amazon had sold over 600 million Alexa-enabled devices worldwide.
You can order a new Echo Dot today for $100, and it comes in four colors (Graphite, Glacier White, Agave Green, and Coral Pink).

articles.headline: Judge rules Trump-appointed US prosecutor in Los Angeles is not serving legally – US politics live
keyFacts: A federal judge has ruled that Republican Bill Essayli is not legally serving as the top US prosecutor in Los Angeles.
Essayli was disqualified from overseeing two criminal prosecutions.
The order, however, will not immediately go into effect, and the Department of Justice (DoJ) has said it intends to appeal.
body: A federal judge has ruled that Republican Bill Essayli is not legally serving as the top US prosecutor in Los Angeles.
Essayli was disqualified from overseeing two criminal prosecutions. The order, however, will not immediately go into effect, and the Department of Justice (DoJ) has said it intends to appeal.
The ruling was part of a long-running legal battle challenging the Trump administration’s maneuvers to keep Essayli in office despite not being confirmed by the US Senate.

Essayli, a former Republican state lawmaker and ally of Donald Trump, became an interim US attorney in April 2025, but he was not formally nominated by the president, which allowed him to lead the office without going through the standard confirmation process.

After Essayli’s “interim” appointment ended last July, the Trump administration gave him an “acting” title, then kept him on as a “first assistant” after a judge ruled he was unlawfully serving as US attorney.

But in August, a federal appellate court ruled against a Nevada justice department leader in a similar case, and the judge overseeing Essayli’s case cited that higher court’s ruling on Tuesday, issuing another order saying he was still acting unlawfully.

Michael Seabright, the federal judge, said Essayli was illegally serving, even with a “special attorney” and “first assistant” designation by the Trump administration, and the judge said he could no longer participate in or supervise two ongoing prosecutions where the attorneys had challenged his position.

“We respectfully disagree with the court’s order,” Essayli said in a statement on Tuesday. “The President and the Attorney General have every right to select supervisors within the Justice Department.”

Faced with widespread voter discontent over the spike in oil prices since he attacked Iran, Donald Trump staged his rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, on Tuesday alongside a vast oil tanker, the Angerona, which the president said had just arrived from Venezuela bearing a personal gift for him: a million barrels of oil.
A senior state department official told the Associated Press that the US will “will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States”.

In his remarks to supporters in Lubbock, Texas, Trump attacked James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for Senate, for having shown compassion for transgender children who demonstrated for their rights at the Texas state capitol in 2023.
Trump lied that “our gasoline prices are lower than when Barack Hussein Obama – our oil prices, gasoline, lower than they were with Obama”.
RFK Jr faces heavy criticism over anti-Arab remarks on campaign trail
Richard Luscombe

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, faced backlash on Wednesday for a “wildly racist tirade” during a campaign stop in Michigan in which he falsely asserted that Arabs never won major awards in science or literature.

Kennedy was speaking at the Monday night event in Grand Rapids in support of Mike Rogers, the Republican US Senate candidate trailing his Democratic midterms opponent Abdul El-Sayed, who is Muslim, in polling.

“There’s 500 million Arabs in the world, and yet they don’t produce science, they don’t win the Nobel prize, they don’t win the Fields prize, they don’t win the Wolf prize, they don’t produce literature,” Kennedy said.
A factcheck published on Tuesday by the Associated Press showed that Arabs have won, or been shortlisted, for all those awards in recent years.

The Council on American-Islamic Relations called Kennedy’s Islamophobic remarks “a textbook display of unvarnished racism and bigotry”, and the US healthcare advocacy organization Protect Our Care condemned his “wildly racist tirade”.
Hillary Scholten, a Democratic congresswoman representing west Michigan, who declined to endorse El-Sayed this summer,said Kennedy’s comments were “disgraceful and have no place in public service”.

In a statement posted to her Facebook page late Tuesday, Scholten said: “As secretary of health and human services, he has a responsibility to serve all Americans, not use his position to demean entire communities with bigoted and demonstrably false claims”.”

She added: “The last I checked, Secretary Kennedy has neither a medical degree nor a Nobel peace prize, and his rhetoric has undermined public confidence in health science. Maybe he should sit this one out.”

Other Trump administration officials have tried to paint El-Sayed as a supporter of Islamic radicalism, including the president himself, who at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday called the Democrat “a jihadist” who was “on the side of the terrorists”.
Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami, having fled to US following Brazilian election defeat

Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of jailed former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro who recently lost the race for his father’s former office, has landed in Miami, apparently taking shelter under the aegis of the Trump administration after fleeing his home country.

The younger Bolsonaro had been ordered to turn over his passport following his election defeat in connection with a criminal investigation over money laundering. Instead, Reuters and other outlets have reported that the defeated candidate and his family fled to Argentina overland before flying to the US via Ecaudor.
He has so far refused to officially concede the race to the victorious left-wing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
Trump has said that Brazilian election appeared “rigged,” but gave little indication he would seek to get involved in disputing the results.

Though Trump did not outright endorse Flavio Bolsonaro, his father Jair was a close ideological ally of Trump’s in Latin America. After Brazil launched a criminal prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro for allegedly attempting a coup to restore him to power after his 2022 election loss, Trump slapped tariffs on the country in retaliation.
And there is little love between Trump and Lula, who has accused Trump of trying to meddle in Brazil’s election in Bolsonaro’s favor.
Republican senator Lisa Murkowski backs Democrat in Alaska governor’s race
Lisa Murkowski, a Republican senator from Alaska, has broken with her party to endorse the Democrat in her state’s gubernatorial contest.

Murkowski, a moderate Republican who is no stranger to breaking with Trump, made her surprise endorsement to local news station KTUU. She told the outlet that she felt the three Republicans contesting Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins in the ranked-choice election lacked the bipartisanship needed for the job, calling them overly partisan.

She said that Kreiss-Tomkins, by contrast, is “a young Alaskan with a view and a perspective that I think Alaska needs right now, a freshness of energy”. She described him as a “a commonsense guy who has a known ability to be working together”.
Trump bound for Ohio, and Vance for North Carolina, with less than a week until the midterms

Donald Trump will return to Ohio on Wednesday to campaign for Republicans in the state, as the GOP looks to hold onto the seat currently occupied by Senator Jon Husted. Husted’s opponent, Sherrod Brown, a former Democratic senator from the state, has a decent lead in the polls with less than a week remaining until election day.
Up until now, Trump has made a habit of praising Husted’s physique (his butt, especially) on the campaign trail. We’ll see if he keeps that up today.

JD Vance, perhaps Trump’s busiest surrogate on the campaign trial, will continue a cross-country air campaign by heading east to North Carolina, where he’ll back Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley, who is trailing in the polls to Democratic former governor Roy Cooper.
Obama to campaign in Georgia alongside Jon Ossoff and Keisha Lance Bottoms

Former president Barack Obama will travel to Georgia tonight to campaign alongside top Democrats in the state, including incumbent senator Jon Ossoff and Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former mayor of Atlanta now seeking the Georgia governor’s office.

Obama has been increasingly active on the campaign trail as the midterms race nears its climax. The former president recently joined rallies in Ohio and Michigan, two states where Democrats are looking to win out closely contested Senate races, before setting his sights on Georgia.

During his previous stop in Ohio, Obama made a jab at Trump for redecorating the White House to look like “Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory”. The remark appeared to get under Trump’s skin, prompting him to respond, and has somehow drawn the restaurant chain into the battle for control of Congress.

In Georgia, Ossoff, who is facing a Senate challenge from Republican House representative Mike Collins, holds a comfortable lead in the polls. Increasingly, the Gerogia Democrat has been seen as a potential contender for the Democrats’ nomination in the 2028 presidential election.
The race is much tighter for Bottoms, who is vying to flip Georgia’s governor’s office red.
Flávio Bolsonaro, defeated rightwing Brazilian presidential candidate, expected to arrive in Miami

Flávio Bolsonaro, the rightwing Brazilian presidential candidate who lost the country’s election to leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is expected to arrive in Miami on Wednesday after fleeing Brazil, Reuters reported.

According to the outlet, Bolsonaro and his family – after crossing by land into Argentina, and from there departing to Ecuador – took a flight bound for the US, where the Trump administration’s state department plans to grant them visas.

Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of Jair Bolsonaro, the Trump-allied former leader of Brazil who was arrested and handed a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup to overturn the result of his own 2022 election defeat to Lula. After his election defeat by Lula over the weekend, and before fleeing to the US, he had been ordered to turn over his passports in connection with a criminal investigation.

Trump did not outright endorse the younger Bolsonaro this time around. But he has publicly sparred with Lula frequently in his second term, including imposing tariffs on Brazil in response to its criminal prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro. And Trump has boasted about his role as an apparent kingmaker in Latin America, where Brazil is one of the few holdouts still controlled by leftwing governments as rightwing leaders are ascendent through the region.
Throughout his re-election campaign, Lula accused the Trump administration of trying to interfere with the vote, and of having colonial ambitions in Brazil.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its last rate-setting meeting before the midterm elections, keeping rates at one of the highest pre-election levels seen in over 20 years.

Last month, Fed officials raised rates for the first time since 2023, citing rising inflation. Inflation has hovered for years above the Fed’s target rate of 2%, and for most of this year, the annualized inflation rate has remained above 3%.
The move infuriated Donald Trump, who said that “interest rates in the United States should be 1% or less”.
Though inflation rose higher in September, going from 3.4% in August to 3.7%, a pause would signal the central bank is taking a wait-and-see approach ahead of the midterms next week.
Interest rates determine the cost of interest for loans, including for credit cards, mortgage and some savings accounts. During times of high inflation, raising rates can slow price increases.
Multiple Fed leaders have suggested in recent weeks that the central bank has room for a pause, even if most Fed economists are predicting one more rate hike before the end of the year.
“The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings, but they should be in place in an acceptable period of time,” Fed governor Christopher Waller said earlier this month.
A federal judge has ruled that Republican Bill Essayli is not legally serving as the top US prosecutor in Los Angeles.
Essayli was disqualified from overseeing two criminal prosecutions. The order, however, will not immediately go into effect, and the Department of Justice (DoJ) has said it intends to appeal.
The ruling was part of a long-running legal battle challenging the Trump administration’s maneuvers to keep Essayli in office despite not being confirmed by the US Senate.

Essayli, a former Republican state lawmaker and ally of Donald Trump, became an interim US attorney in April 2025, but he was not formally nominated by the president, which allowed him to lead the office without going through the standard confirmation process.

After Essayli’s “interim” appointment ended last July, the Trump administration gave him an “acting” title, then kept him on as a “first assistant” after a judge ruled he was unlawfully serving as US attorney.

But in August, a federal appellate court ruled against a Nevada justice department leader in a similar case, and the judge overseeing Essayli’s case cited that higher court’s ruling on Tuesday, issuing another order saying he was still acting unlawfully.

Michael Seabright, the federal judge, said Essayli was illegally serving, even with a “special attorney” and “first assistant” designation by the Trump administration, and the judge said he could no longer participate in or supervise two ongoing prosecutions where the attorneys had challenged his position.

“We respectfully disagree with the court’s order,” Essayli said in a statement on Tuesday. “The President and the Attorney General have every right to select supervisors within the Justice Department.”

Faced with widespread voter discontent over the spike in oil prices since he attacked Iran, Donald Trump staged his rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, on Tuesday alongside a vast oil tanker, the Angerona, which the president said had just arrived from Venezuela bearing a personal gift for him: a million barrels of oil.
A senior state department official told the Associated Press that the US will “will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States”.

In his remarks to supporters in Lubbock, Texas, Trump attacked James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for Senate, for having shown compassion for transgender children who demonstrated for their rights at the Texas state capitol in 2023.
Trump lied that “our gasoline prices are lower than when Barack Hussein Obama – our oil prices, gasoline, lower than they were with Obama”.

articles.headline: Everything We Saw At Nintendo’s October Indie World Showcase
keyFacts: Nintendo hosted an Indie World showcase highlighting various independent video games coming to the Switch and Switch 2 consoles.
Featured titles included upcoming releases like Witchbrook, Sword of the Sea, Slime Rancher 2, and numerous others with varying release dates.
Several games launched demo versions on the eShop on the same day as the presentation.
body: Nintendo held another Indie World showcase this morning, putting a spotlight on independent projects coming to the Switch and Switch 2, and though the presentation was short, it was packed full of cool games coming to the handheld consoles. If you weren’t able to watch the showcase live, you can check out the VOD below, but if you just want to scroll through the highlights, read on.
Witchbrook
Kicking things off is Witchbrook, a magical, town-building social sim coming to Switch and Switch 2 on January 28.
Winds of Viridia

Keeping with the fantasy theme, next up isÂ Winds of Viridia, an action survival game in a “vast, seamless” world where you’ll fight monsters and try to survive the dangers of the wild. A demo will be available later today, with the full game coming early next year.
City of None
City of None is a new puzzle-platformer from one of the co-creators ofÂ Celeste. The game is coming to Switch and Switch 2 next year.
Sword of the Sea
TheÂ Journey-esqueÂ Sword of the Sea, which is coming out tomorrow, October 29, got a brief trailer showing its gorgeous desert levels.
Tenjutsu
Next up isÂ Tenjutsu from Deepnight Games, led by the lead designer of Dead Cells. The rougelike brawler is inspired by classic anime aesthetics and is coming to Switch 2 next year.
Threads of Time

If you’re looking for something less action-oriented and more strategic,Â Threads of Time looks like a throwback to the SNES-era Final Fantasy games, and it’s coming to Switch and Switch 2 next summer.
Dumpster Gang
Next up isÂ Dumpster Gang, in which a group of up to four players play as raccoons trying to live their chaotic lives as trash pandas while avoiding animal control. It’s coming to Switch 2 in March.
Super Battle Golf

Up to eight players can play a ridiculous, action-oriented golf match inÂ Super Battle Golf, in which you can use tools like a rocket launcher and motorcycle instead of simply using a golf club. It’s coming to Switch 2 on March 25.
R.E.P.O.
Co-op horror gameÂ R.E.P.O.Â has players extracting items from procedurally generated haunted houses, and it’s coming to Switch 2 next year.
Haunted Paws

Haunted PawsÂ is a Switch and Switch 2 co-op game in which you and a friend play as cute puppies trying to rescue someone from a haunted mansion by solving puzzles, playing mini-games, and hiding from spooky foes. A demo is out on the eShop today.
Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino
Next up isÂ Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino, an adventure game set in a fantastical Japan coming to Switch 2 next spring.
Slime Rancher 2
For a palate cleanser after all those spooky vibes, we have Slime Rancher 2. The puzzle shooter is coming to Switch 2 in January.
Spirit Crossing

The makers ofÂ Cozy Grove are makingÂ Spirit Crossing, an MMO life sim in which you and your friends can work together to build homes and community. The game is coming to Switch and Switch 2 on November 16 as a console exclusive.
My Arms Are Longer Now

Toot Games showed offÂ My Arms Are Longer Now, a humorous puzzler about an endlessly long arm that is kinda gross but also, in my experience playing it at Summer Game Fest this year, pretty funny. It’s coming to Switch and Switch 2 on March 11.
Petal Runner
Petal Runner is a Game Boyâinspired retro RPG about “life and loss” coming to Switch 2 on March 8, and it has a demo available today.
Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition
Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition, the new edition of the “coin pusher roguelike,” is coming to Switch 2 and supports mouse controls. It’s coming to the system on November 10. A demo is available today.
Montage
The show closed out with a montage of a handful of indie games:
- Tanuki: Pon’s Summer, launching November 10
- Finding Polka, launching next spring
- Floor Plan: Slap Out of It!, launching next spring
- Lost and Found Co., launching early 2027
